questions.question: Explain why African farmers settled east of the 500 mm rainfall line.
questions.expected_answer: Their main crops, sorghum and millet, grow in the hot, wet summer and need at least about 500 mm of rain in the growing season. Rainfall in South Africa decreases from east to west, and most of the country has summer rain, except the south-western Cape (winter rain). East of the 500 mm line dryland crop farming is possible; west of it is too dry, and the winter-rain Cape does not suit summer crops. So farmers settled in the summer rainfall areas of the east.

questions.question: Describe the way of life of African farmers.
questions.expected_answer: Bantu-speaking Iron Age farmers who arrived about 2000 years ago; lived in settled villages/homesteads arranged around a central cattle kraal; grew sorghum, millet, beans, pumpkins (women did much of the cultivation); stored grain in granaries/pits; kept cattle, sheep and goats - cattle meant wealth, milk, lobola and ceremonies; worked iron and copper; organised in chiefdoms where the chief allocated communal land; traded with others including the San and Khoikhoi.

questions.question: Why did contact between trekboers and Xhosa farmers lead to competition?
questions.expected_answer: Both were cattle farmers needing the same summer grazing land and water in the Zuurveld (between the Bushmans and Fish rivers) when trekboers moved east in the 1770s; they had different ideas about land (communal allocation vs private ownership); this led to trade but also to disputes over cattle and land and to the frontier wars from 1779.
